Definition: from G1909 and G2476; to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal); --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over).
BiblicalUsage: Ephistemi means to stand upon, to be present, to come suddenly. The angel of the Lord came upon the shepherds; Martha was cumbered about much serving and came to Jesus; the angel stood by Peter in prison; the Lord stood by Paul in the night; and Timothy is told to be instant in season and out of season.
TheologicalSignificance: God stands by His people suddenly, and His people are to stand by their calling constantly. I believe the two truths belong together: the angel in the prison, the Lord in the night, and Timothy told to be instant in season and out of season.
